title: Settlement of a Medicare Supplement Premium Account in Arrears
content:
Where a policyholder asks what must reach the plan to bring their premium account under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies up to date, the figure is the premium owed for the billing period now current, together with the charges standing on the account for the periods the settlement reaches back over and the policy fee falling due with it, less the money already standing to the policyholder's credit.

The amount a policyholder must pay to bring the account up to date is not fixed before the premium account carries the return owed on premium charged for months in which other Medicare coverage was still in force. Until such a return stands on that account, the figure is not settled.

Paying the money onto the account is the policyholder's own act. The payment is applied to the billing period it names, the account shows the payment against that period, and the outstanding balance the account shows falls by what has been paid.

## Taking the payment

The payment is made with `remit_supplement_settlement_23b5df61`, which is the policyholder's own tool: the representative unlocks it and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves over the telephone. One call hands over one payment, and the money leaves the card or bank account the policyholder is paying from.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form it takes |
|---|---|---|
| `medigap_policy_id` | The reference number of the Medicare Supplement policy the money is being paid onto, read from the policy record held for the policyholder | An identifier |
| `customer_id` | The policyholder's own member reference number, read from their member profile | An identifier |
| `medigap_premium_entry_id` | The reference number of the premium account entry the money is applied against, read from the entries on that policy's premium account | An identifier |
| `billing_period` | The first month of the billing span the money is applied to | Written as YYYY-MM |
| `settlement_amount` | The money being paid now, in USD | Recorded to 2 decimal places and never negative |
| `balance_effect` | What this payment does to the balance the premium account shows once it is applied | One of four values, set out below |
| `remittance_reference` | The payment reference printed on the premium notice being paid from | Copied character for character exactly as written there, keeping the original wording, digits and punctuation, with nothing translated, normalised, summarised, added or dropped |

The four values `balance_effect` takes are `not_applicable`, where the entry is of a kind that moves no balance at all; `partial_payment`, where the money leaves part of what the account shows outstanding still unpaid; `settles_balance`, where the money brings the account exactly to nothing owed; and `overpayment`, where the money is more than the account shows outstanding and leaves a credit standing.

### What comes back

A confirmation sentence in plain text naming the reference number of the payment entry now on the premium account, the policy it was paid onto, the amount taken and the billing period it was applied to. Receiving that sentence is what says the money has been taken and posted; no other value is returned.
